localChanges: A city of size 1 no longer destroys itself by completing Settlers. It now waits, and completes them on the turn it grows to size 2. The city screen says so before you pay for them and while the city waits, and the cities list and map banner no longer show “1 turn” for a city that is waiting. Games already in progress get this too (#959).

That is a new Enhanced rule you can untick when starting a game. Unticked, the game follows the original: on Chieftain the city waits; on other levels your only city builds the Settlers and stays at size 1, and any other city is given up, leaving the Settlers on its square.

Four more Enhanced rules can be switched when starting a game. Two are ticked by default and keep play as it was: the United Nations stops computer players going to war with its owner, and every advance a Diplomat could steal is equally likely. Two are new and unticked by default: SDI Defence spares its city from a nuclear attack, and bribed and defecting units stay veteran (#960).

log: Two rule sets that are on by default carry today's play, now that the Civ1 packages hold v474.05's: the United Nations stops computer players going to war with a computer owner, and every advance a Diplomat could steal is equally likely.
Two new variants are off by default: a city with SDI Defense is not halved by a nuclear attack, and a unit that is bribed or defects with its city keeps its veteran status.
Each supersedes the original's rule by its exported id (civ-clone/web-renderer#960, part of #954). Needs civ1-unit 0.1.27 and civ1-wonder 0.1.10.

A new rule set, on by default: Settlers in a city of size 1 are held, at every level, until the city grows to size 2, and are completed on that turn. The reason is given from the moment they are chosen (`CityBuild#held()`), so a client can say the build will wait. It supersedes civ1-unit's Chieftain rule; switched off, the original's three cases apply (civ-clone/web-renderer#959, part of #954).
Before, a city of size 1 that completed Settlers was destroyed and the Settlers with it. Needs @civ-clone/core-city-build 0.1.21 and civ1-unit 0.1.27.

Stealing an advance walks v474.05's list of 72 advances from one random place (DIPLOMAT.C), so the draw is always made, the Barbarians take nothing and nothing is taken from them. Today's rule, where every advance is equally likely, moves to civ1-enhanced as a rule set that is on by default.

The rules that halve the cities a nuclear attack reaches and that make a unit that changes sides start afresh have ids exported from `RuleIds`, fixed priorities, and their code in `lib/nuclear` and `lib/startAfresh`, so civ1-enhanced can offer variants of them (civ-clone/web-renderer#960, part of #954).

A city of size 1 that completes Settlers now does what v474.05 does (CITYMGT.C 581-606). On Chieftain the build is held, for computer players too, through `core-city-build`'s new `Hold` rules. On other levels a player's only city builds them and stays at size 1, and a city with others is removed, leaving the Settlers on its square with the player's nearest city as their home and no veteran status. Before, the city and its Settlers were both destroyed at every level.

civ1-enhanced adds a rule set, on by default, that holds the Settlers until the city is size 2 at every level (civ-clone/web-renderer#959, part of #954). What still differs from v474.05 is in civ-clone/web-renderer#969.

The United Nations' rule now needs its owner to be a human player: v474.05 asks about it only in the human's parley (AUDIENCE.C), never when two computer players meet (DIPLOMAC.C, which asks only about the Great Wall). Today's rule, which also stops computer players going to war with a computer owner, moves to civ1-enhanced as a rule set that is on by default (civ-clone/web-renderer#960, part of #954). The rule's id is exported from `RuleIds`.
Also drops the unused base-city-yield-research dependency.

A new rule type, `Hold`, keeps a city from completing what it is building while the rule's criteria are met: the item stays chosen, its progress stays and goes on growing, and nothing is announced, until a turn on which nothing holds it. `CityBuild#held()` gives the ids of the rules holding the item being built, whatever its progress, and is sent with each build, so a client can say a build will wait before it is paid for and that it is waiting once it is (civ-clone/web-renderer#959).
With no `Hold` rule registered nothing changes.
